upgrades.name: Denoising-time repair schedule (annealed strength + ramped margin, full enforcement late)
upgrades.source_methods: SafeDiffuser ReS/TVS (ICLR25), TouchGuide k/(1-k) late ramp, Kynkaanniemi guidance-interval (NeurIPS24), FK-Flow harmonic down-weighting, QPILOTS never-at-t=0; SafeFlowMatcher slack w_t -> 0
upgrades.what_changes_in_our_code: pi0_guided.py: body(_, carry) currently discards the fori_loop index — pass k into _dcbf_repair. Add two length-num_steps jnp arrays to GuidanceParams (shape-static, no recompiles): repair_weight[k] and margin_scale[k]. In repair_one.body use new_step = disp_acc[j] + repair_weight[k]*deficit*direction and r_j = margin_scale[k]*(r_eff + inflation_slope*(j+1)). Default schedule: repair_weight = 0 for k in {0,1}, ramp over k=2..6 (TVS-style margin ramp or TouchGuide t/(1-t) normalized), = 1.0 for k >= 7 so the last 3 steps and the terminal chunk satisfy the exact chain — terminal guarantee unchanged. One jitted code path preserved via the existing enabled-blend pattern.
upgrades.expected_benefit: L1-fat TSR 58.5 -> ~70-75 at held CAR: removes the SafeDiffuser-RoS mode-locking pattern (41-100% documented trap rates for always-hard enforcement; ITPS shows per-step projection = repeated output perturbation, exactly our TSR/CAR signature). Second-order effect is the big one: recovered TSR headroom lets us run the fat envelope (CAR 44.5) or fatter everywhere, converting schedule slack directly into CAR. Three independent 2025-26 systems converge on this schedule; it is the single most evidence-backed change we can make.
upgrades.cost_days: 1-2 (0.5 impl, rest = grid sweep {cutoff k0, ramp shape} on Spatial L2 with held-out seeds)
upgrades.risk: Low. Final-step full-strength repair preserves the terminal chain certificate; only risk is hyperparameter tuning discipline — pre-register the grid, tune on L2, report L1 untouched.

upgrades.name: Brake-then-push repair channel with clamp-feasible fallback (retiming before radial displacement)
upgrades.source_methods: PC-Diffuser (velocity-channel-only corrections beat all three SafeDiffuser variants, 10.3% vs 74-89% residual collisions), PolyFlow discretization-violation warning
upgrades.what_changes_in_our_code: In repair_one.body, when deficit > 0: first shrink the approach component of disp_acc[j] (project out max(dot(step, -direction), 0), i.e., slow/stop motion toward the obstacle), then apply radial push only for the remaining deficit. Critically, if jnp.clip saturates the per-step |command|<=1 bound, fall back to full brake (zero the toward-obstacle displacement): for our single-integrator rollout braking always yields B_j >= B_{j-1} - inflation_slope, so chain feasibility under actuation limits becomes guaranteed rather than best-effort. Keep the residual diagnostic; expect max_residual -> ~0. Fully jnp, ~15 lines inside the existing fori_loop.
upgrades.expected_benefit: CAR direct: kills the executed-with-residual failure mode (currently a silent hard-guarantee hole — clamp-saturated repairs are executed anyway). Estimated CAR +10-20 on L1/L2 where repairs are large (near-target). TSR neutral-to-positive: retiming preserves the learned path geometry instead of shearing it sideways, PC-Diffuser's core finding. Also strengthens the paper's guarantee claim: chain feasibility holds under the command clamp, provable in one paragraph.
upgrades.risk: Low. Braking can stall progress when the obstacle sits on the only approach — mitigated by the corridor exemption (below) and chunk-boundary replanning; report stall rate honestly.

upgrades.name: Batched best-of-K seeds + lexicographic terminal acceptance on the executed 5-step prefix
upgrades.source_methods: ITPS (sampling = least distribution shift per unit alignment), Ma et al. CVPR25 inference-time scaling, RoboMonkey/MG-Select selection family, SafeFlowMatcher executed-path-only principle, FK-Steering (terminal-only = the degenerate-FK baseline we start from)
upgrades.what_changes_in_our_code: guided_policy.py infer(): the model code is already batch-first; replace the [np.newaxis] batch=1 pin with K-way tiling. Compute prefix_tokens/kv_cache ONCE from the single observation, then jnp.repeat the kv_cache and masks along batch so only the suffix forward is K-batched (makes K=8 ~2-3x latency, not 8x). Draw K noises with a temperature knob tau (diversity is mandatory — deterministic 10-step Euler means seed fully determines chunk). Diagnostics are already (B,)-shaped; add a jittable selector: feasible = executed-prefix (first 5 steps) chain satisfaction with inflated margins; among feasible, argmax(min-margin, then progress-toward-target from the guidance payload); if none feasible, argmax margin then hard-repair that one. Pure jnp argmax — no host callback. Report NFEs and latency per chunk honestly.
upgrades.expected_benefit: CAR +10-15: the executed prefix is what actually collides, and selection finds seeds whose prefix is feasible with margin to spare under open-loop tracking error — directly attacking the L2 CAR 49 gap. TSR held or improved (selection cannot leave the manifold; ITPS ranks it best on alignment-vs-shift). Also yields the paper's certificate story: every executed prefix passes an explicit inflated-margin acceptance test. This is planned P4 — the upgrade over the plan is the shared-kv-cache batching and the lexicographic feasible->margin+progress ordering with safety strictly first (neutralizes verifier-hacking on the progress term).
upgrades.cost_days: 2-3 (1 batching + cache broadcast, 1 selector + diag plumbing, 1 K/tau sweep)
upgrades.risk: Low-medium: GPU memory at K=8 with the 3B model (drop to K=4 if needed — FK-Steering shows k=2-8 suffices); latency must be reported (+2-3x per chunk).

upgrades.name: Soft hinge-gradient pre-shaping on the x1-prediction, mid steps only (standardized robust recipe)
upgrades.source_methods: QGF (identity Jacobian, detached velocity net), QPILOTS-U (Tweedie eval, magnitude rescale to ||v||, skip first step), VGG-Flow (training-free value-gradient form, preserves prior fidelity), Feng et al. 2502.02150 (x1-prediction gradients, softened hinge), OmniGuide (clipped collision repeller composes with other stages), Adaptive-SOC (strength scales with actual violation)
upgrades.what_changes_in_our_code: pi0_guided.py: have euler_step return v_t; compute the clean prediction x1_hat = x_t + time*(-v_t)*sign-corrected per openpi's t:1->0 convention (validate against final output on unguided runs first). Define E = sum_j softplus_beta((1-gamma)B_{j-1} - B_j) on the translational rollout of x1_hat — reuse the existing _closest/cumsum machinery, so jax.grad(E) differentiates ONLY our analytic rollout, never PaliGemma (zero extra NFEs, trivially jittable). Apply with identity Jacobian: v_guided = v_t - eta_k * (||v_t||/(||g||+eps)) * clip(g), with eta_k a length-num_steps array active on steps ~2-7 (composes with the schedule upgrade: soft mid, hard late).
upgrades.expected_benefit: L1 TSR +5-8: chunks arrive at the late hard sweep already near-feasible, so repair magnitudes (correction_norm diag) shrink and manifold shear drops — VGG-Flow shows this form preserves prior fidelity, OmniGuide's ablation shows denoise-guidance alone gives +20% success/-34% collisions and composes with other stages. Secondary CAR +3-7 from steering the mode/homotopy choice mid-trajectory instead of fighting it late. Cheap to verify: correction_norm at steps 7-10 should visibly fall.
upgrades.risk: Medium-low: one new knob eta (largely self-tuning via magnitude rescale); time-convention bug risk on x1_hat — mitigated by the unguided-run validation test. No guarantee claims attach to this stage, so honest-reporting exposure is nil.

upgrades.name: P3 semantic corridor as attractor + anisotropic margin exemption (not margin-only)
upgrades.source_methods: OmniGuide Gaussian semantic attractor (lambda_S:lambda_C ~ 250:1) , DynaGuide logsumexp goal-set (smooth corridor basin), Adaptive-SOC automatic relaxation near sanctioned regions, mirror-map corridor-coordinates idea (2510.08929) as inspiration only
upgrades.what_changes_in_our_code: Extend GuidanceParams with target_pos and approach_axis (client sends GT target in P3/P4, VLM in P5). Two coupled changes: (a) hard-sweep side — scale deficit by (1 - c*cone(p_j; target, axis, half_angle)) so margins relax only inside the sanctioned approach cone (anisotropic r_eff, ~10 lines in repair_one); (b) soft side — add the attractor term -||p_H - target||^2 (or logsumexp over poses along the approach path) into the pre-shaping energy E with weight ratio ~100:1 over the repeller per OmniGuide's tuning. Keep the executed-prefix acceptance test's exemption geometry identical to the sweep's so the certificate statement stays consistent. Honest reporting: corridor contacts still count against CAR; report cone geometry in the paper.
upgrades.expected_benefit: This is the targeted fix for L1 = obstacle-near-target, where the thin/fat envelope tradeoff (71.0/23.5 vs 58.5/44.5) exists precisely because a uniform envelope cannot distinguish sanctioned approach from hazard approach. Combined with the schedule + brake-channel upgrades, target L1 >= 75 TSR at >= 60 CAR — past the SOTA competitor's admitted weak spot (their Spatial L1-analog Level II TSR 70%, Object CAR 46% from clearance underestimation).
upgrades.risk: Medium: a wrongly-oriented corridor punches a hole in the envelope. In P3/P4 the corridor comes from GT (low risk); in P5 gate the exemption by perception confidence (see P1 item). Cone half-angle is a new hyperparameter — pre-register and ablate.
upgrades.priority: P0 (do in Phase 3/4 — this IS Phase 3)

upgrades.name: FK mid-trajectory resampling with drift-corrected noise injection (upgrade best-of-K to particles)
upgrades.source_methods: FK-Flow 2509.01543 (score-from-velocity for Gaussian-source CFM, harmonic schedule, soft potentials only), FK-Steering ICML25 (k=2-8, interval resampling), VLS (FK on action chunks + RBF repulsion), TDS lesson (twists unreliable early), BayesFP (validates FK at pi0.5 scale — also our ablation baseline)
upgrades.what_changes_in_our_code: On top of the batched sampler: inside the fori_loop convert the ODE to a marginal-preserving SDE — v_drift = v_t + (sigma_k^2/2)*s_t with the score expressed analytically from v_t for the linear interpolant (one line once the time convention is validated), plus sigma_k*sqrt(dt)*noise via a folded PRNG key. At 2 steps (k=4,7) compute weights exp(-lambda*hinge_energy(x1_hat rollout)) with harmonic early down-weighting, resample particle indices with jax.random.categorical + jnp.take along batch (jittable gather; kv_cache is shared so no cache shuffling needed). Terminal lexicographic selection unchanged. Soft signed-margin potential ONLY — never the 0/1 feasibility indicator (FK-Flow's documented failure mode).
upgrades.expected_benefit: CAR +3-8 over terminal-only best-of-K at equal K: kills doomed seeds mid-run and reallocates NFEs where the feasible set is thin (L1). Only worth building if the P0 batched selector shows feasible-seed starvation (log the feasible-count-per-chunk histogram first — that diagnostic is free). Also the honest differentiator vs BayesFP: their FK tilt without our hard layer becomes our soft-only ablation row.
upgrades.cost_days: 3-4 (1 SDE conversion + marginal-preservation validation on unguided TSR, 1-2 resampler, 1 lambda/schedule sweep)
upgrades.risk: Medium-high: SDE conversion correctness at 10 Euler steps (validate that unguided TSR is unchanged under noise injection BEFORE claiming anything — honest-reporting gate); if injection degrades quality, do NOT build GLASS — fall back to terminal-only selection.

upgrades.name: Gauss-Seidel multi-pass sweep with backward anticipation pass (approximate joint min-norm)
upgrades.source_methods: Competitor 2607.01378 (joint SLSQP over all H constraints distributes correction — plausibly their chunk-shape edge), PC-Diffuser path-shape preservation
upgrades.what_changes_in_our_code: Wrap repair_one's inner fori_loop in an outer fori_loop of 2-3 passes; add a backward pass that shrinks approach components of steps j-2..j-1 preceding a violation at j, so correction spreads over waypoints instead of dumping entirely on the first violating step. Shape-static, fully jittable, no solver.
upgrades.expected_benefit: TSR +2-5 on L1 via less path distortion per unit repair; removes a structural asymmetry vs the SOTA competitor (our in-order sweep vs their joint solve), enabling a clean sweep-vs-joint ablation table in the paper.
upgrades.risk: Low; convergence of the Gauss-Seidel passes is monotone for our chain structure.
upgrades.priority: P1 (Phase 5-6; run as ablation even if P0 stack already wins)

upgrades.name: Perception-confidence gating + residual-adaptive margin inflation for P5
upgrades.source_methods: GAF ensemble-disagreement gate exp(-alpha*sigma), Feedback-WM online prediction-residual feedback (principled adaptive margin), FK-Flow soft-potential lesson
upgrades.what_changes_in_our_code: Client-side at chunk boundaries (host callback explicitly allowed here): maintain a running residual between predicted clearance (previous chunk's min_clearance diag — already returned) and observed EEF clearance from the simulator/RGB-D; set inflation_slope = base + L*residual (Luenberger-style gain, clipped). Gate the corridor exemption strength c and margin relaxation by VLM constraint confidence (vote entropy from our existing multi-prompt majority-voting pipeline): confident -> full exemption + tight margins; uncertain -> exemption off, margins inflated. Server-side these are just the existing GuidanceParams scalars — zero sampler changes.
upgrades.expected_benefit: This is what makes P5 (VLM+RGB-D, default-deny occupancy) land without either CAR collapse (perception misses) or TSR collapse (false-positive envelopes) — GAF's core finding is that ungated guidance under distribution shift goes negative. Protects the GT->perception transition that the SOTA competitor never attempts, which is our headline scope advantage.
upgrades.risk: Low (client-side only, no jit impact); gain L needs one tuning pass.

upgrades.name: Recurrence after repair (matched re-noise + one extra velocity step, M=2 on middle steps)
upgrades.source_methods: TFG recurrence (most robust knob across 16 tasks), ITPS annealed-MCMC inner loop, DynaGuide M-repeat stabilization, ViTaL partial re-noise edit
upgrades.what_changes_in_our_code: At steps k=5,7 after _dcbf_repair: add sigma_k-matched Gaussian noise to x_t and run one extra euler_step at the same time value before continuing (+20% NFEs, jittable, folded PRNG). Equivalently ViTaL-style: after terminal selection, re-noise the winner to t~0.7 and re-denoise 3 steps under the scheduled sweep to polish residual violations within the winning mode.
upgrades.expected_benefit: TSR +2-5 by letting the frozen policy re-attract repaired chunks to its manifold — but likely partly redundant once the schedule removes early hard repairs. Build only if the P0 stack leaves an L1 TSR gap; otherwise it is one ablation row demonstrating we tested the standard manifold-healing knob.
upgrades.risk: Low-medium: +20% latency; interacts with the schedule (tune jointly or report interaction).

upgrades.name: FRS reversed-repaired informed seed (repair once at clean level, reverse-flow to noise, re-denoise)
upgrades.source_methods: Flow Reversal Steering 2606.13675, ViTaL anchor-edit outer/inner decomposition
upgrades.what_changes_in_our_code: New jitted routine: run one unguided 10-step forward pass, apply _dcbf_repair once to the clean chunk, integrate the ODE backward 10 steps (x -= dt*v with time reversed) to obtain an informed noise seed, insert it as 1 of the K seeds in the batched sampler. ~2x flow cost for that one seed; selection stays lexicographic.
upgrades.expected_benefit: Targets exactly L1-fat where random seeds are rarely feasible: the round trip produces a chunk that is simultaneously near-feasible and in-distribution (FRS's deliberate reconstruction bias), replacing 10 accumulating projections with one repair + one round trip. If it works it is a distinctive paper element; if not, it costs one ablation row.
upgrades.risk: Medium: reverse-integration fidelity at 10 steps is unproven for pi0.5; benefit overlaps with FK resampling.

upgrades.name: MG-Select masked-conditioning KL as the progress tiebreaker
upgrades.source_methods: MG-Select (ICLR26, verifier-free confidence via KL between full and masked-conditioning action distributions)
upgrades.what_changes_in_our_code: For the top feasible candidates from the batched selector, run extra suffix forwards with language/state conditioning masked and score by KL from the full-conditioning velocity — a policy-native progress signal replacing the hand-coded displacement-toward-target term, kept lexicographically second behind safety.
upgrades.expected_benefit: Cleaner progress ranking among feasible seeds (their +28% ID gains suggest a few TSR points), but our GT progress term is adequate for ICRA and this adds forward passes and engineering.
upgrades.risk: Medium: extra latency; masking pi0.5's conditioning path needs model surgery.

do_not_adopt: 1) PolyFlow / Mirror / Reflected / chance-constrained FM (constraint-embedded flows): require retraining and constraint sets that are convex and known at training time — we have a frozen pi0.5 and per-episode, non-convex, perception-derived constraint sets. Cite as positioning ('constraint embedding cannot handle inference-time semantic constraints'), nothing more. 2) Learned safety critics/verifiers (QPILOTS SARSA critic, GAF chunk critics, RoboMonkey verifier fine-tuning, DynaGuide dynamics model, TouchGuide contact model): training burden inside the 9-week runway; GAF shows near-zero OOD transfer (+2.5pp held-out, negative on spatial transfer); and honest-reporting hazard — training rollout-scorers on the same 50-episode suites we evaluate on invites contamination. Our geometric barrier under GT/perception state is exact; a learned proxy is strictly worse on the safety axis. 3) Fisher-Preserving Guidance Jacobian projection: needs input-output Jacobians of the 3B kv-cached PaliGemma denoiser per step — heavy backward passes that break our cheap-jitted-loop budget; TFG recurrence captures most of the manifold-drift benefit at near-zero engineering, so recurrence is the sanctioned proxy. 4) GLASS Flows inner-flow transitions: second-line fallback only if FK noise injection measurably degrades unguided TSR — do not build preemptively. 5) Psi-Sampler pCNL noise-space MCMC: the x1-prediction at t~1 is nearly the chunk mean, so its gradients are uninformative exactly where pCNL operates; adds burn-in latency; zero-order perturbation around the best feasible seed (Ma et al.) achieves the same inside the batched selector for free. 6) Full twisted-SMC / trust-region / tree samplers (TDS/DTS lineage): built for hundreds of denoising steps and stiff likelihoods; at 10 Euler steps and K<=8 single-pass FK is the right operating point — anything more is unjustifiable compute and paper-review risk. 7) BayesFP machinery wholesale: it is our closest competitor and our soft-only ablation row; adopting it duplicates FK resampling while lacking the hard layer that differentiates us. 8) Learned/Girsanov-trained adaptive guidance strength (Adaptive-SOC): adopt only the closed-form structure (strength proportional to violation over gradient norm) inside the soft pre-shaping stage; no learned controller. 9) Hard indicator potentials in any particle weight (FK-Flow's documented failure) and raw-x_t gradients (Feng et al.'s worst case) — both are tempting shortcuts our stiff barrier invites; use softened hinges on x1-predictions everywhere. 10) Any fine-tuning of pi0.5 — violates the frozen-policy premise that defines the paper.
verdict: Projection-per-Euler-step survives as the backbone, but demoted from "the method" to "the enforcement stage" — and the literature is strikingly consistent about how. Our uniform full-strength repair at every step from t=1 is the SafeDiffuser-RoS anti-pattern: three independent lines (PolyFlow, SafeFlowMatcher, ITPS) document that it maximizes constraint compliance while minimizing execution quality, which is precisely our L1-fat signature and the thin/fat tradeoff. The fix is not to abandon the sweep but to schedule it (untouched steps 0-1, soft x1-hinge gradients mid, full-strength sweep late) and wrap it in an escalation ordered by distribution shift: select seeds first, guide second, project last, certify the executed 5-step prefix always. Against the three alternatives: (a) SMC/particle steering alone is exact only in distribution — no per-rollout guarantee, and on a deterministic 10-step Euler chain it needs noise-injection machinery of unproven fidelity; it enters as a P1 upgrade inside best-of-K, not a backbone. (b) Executed-path-only correction (SafeFlowMatcher pure form) discards in-generation adaptation, which demonstrably works for us (L2 TSR 86.5 vs baseline 55.5) and for the SOTA competitor; it contributes the terminal certificate and finite-time convergence term, not the architecture. (c) Gradient pre-shaping + terminal projection is strictly contained in the scheduled design — terminal-only projection concentrates correction into one large last-step shear, the exact manifold-drift mechanism we're trying to eliminate. Decisive practical point: our jitted in-order sweep is the only component in either survey that is simultaneously shape-static, host-callback-free, and cheap enough to run per-step, per-particle, and at the terminal certificate; every P0 upgrade is a parameter-schedule or batching change inside the same fori_loop. And the composition — scheduled soft pre-shaping + late hard DCBF sweep + seed selection + executed-prefix certificate on a frozen 3B VLA — is occupied by nobody (BayesFP lacks the hard layer; the SLSQP competitor lacks schedules, seeds, and corridors). That composition is the ICRA paper; the backbone stays.
